adaptation: TypeScript -> plain ESM JavaScript. The port is a transcription of the donor's own compiled output (lib/**, the executable golden oracle) cross-checked against src/**, with the type surface expressed as JSDoc @param/@returns and `readonly`/`as const` expressed as Object.freeze where the donor froze at runtime.

Import graph flattened: the donor's `types/{metrics,provider,window,decision,config,index}.ts` collapse into one `types.mjs`; the eight `providers/*.ts` collapse into one `providers.mjs`. Three donor-private module constants named `PROVIDES` became HARDWARE_PROVIDES / MEMORY_PROVIDES / RUNTIME_PROVIDES because they now share one scope; nothing else was renamed.

Four donor module-private functions were promoted to exports so the module is testable through one entry point and the donor's own test vectors remain expressible: `bandKeyOf`, `rampEndpoints`, `clamp`, `byScoreDescending` (bands), `parseSampleTime` (normalize), `startOfLocalDay` (maintenance), `cooldownKindOf` / `cooldownMsOf` / `initialActionAttempts` (policy), `ProcessTreeReader`, `parseTasklistMemoryLine`, `parsePsMemoryLine`, `mergeHardwareMetrics`, `formatBytes`/`formatDelta`/`formatSlopePerHour` (already public), `renderMetricRow` and the three report sections. No behaviour was added.

The donor's `src/dsh/report.ts` presentation module is carried over as report.mjs. It is pure functions over a snapshot and had no Cordis dependency: `metricsSnapshot`, `renderHealthReport`, `renderMetricRow`. The three section renderers from `src/dsh/plugin.ts` (`renderPressureSection`, `renderMaintenanceSection`, `renderProviderSection`) are pure too and moved here with it.

The donor's settings *registration* is Cordis binding and is dropped; the logic behind it is kept as settings.mjs. `SETTINGS_NAMESPACE` and the declarative `configSchema()` are carried over as data, and the watch-callback behaviour becomes the pure `applySettingsUpdate(scheduler, next)`: re-resolve the whole document with the authoritative validator, then `scheduler.reconfigure(resolved)`; on failure change nothing and return the ConfigError. That is the donor's rule that a value the UI accepts but the engine cannot act on is rejected loudly instead of silently applied.

The donor's provider graph projection is kept as wiring.mjs (`buildBuiltInProviders` / `registerBuiltInProviders`), ported verbatim from `registerBuiltInProviders` in `src/dsh/plugin.ts`. It never read `ctx`, so only its signature changed: it now takes the environment and returns the providers as well as registering them. Both donor quirks are preserved: the memory provider is fed the *hardware* helper command, and the ProcessTreeReader is built only when extraPids is non-empty.

`src/dsh/context.ts` is dropped entirely. It existed only to structurally type the Cordis context the plugin read (`ctx.tools`, `ctx.settings`, `ctx.logger`, `ctx.effect`, `ctx.healthScheduler`). Nothing in the ported engine referenced it.
The donor's `presets/*.json` are embedded verbatim as `PRESET_DOCUMENTS` so an operator can diff the numbers without reading the scaling code. They are asserted equal to the presets the code builds.

`src/index.ts` exports `apply`, `name`, `inject` and `applyHealthScheduler`. All four are Cordis binding and are dropped. `createScheduler` is kept: it is pure construction. Every other member of the donor's `lib/index.js` export list is republished from index.mjs, so the dropped four are the only omissions.
The donor's `lib/` build output is not shipped and there is no build step. The module is plain `.mjs`, discovered and run by `node city/test-all.mjs`.

House style: 2-space indentation (the donor's compiled 4-space output was re-indented), `Object.freeze` on exported constant tables, `node:`-prefixed built-in imports only, and a UTOPIA header on every file that keeps the donor's own explanatory prose.
knownDifferences: No plugin entry point. There is no `apply`, no `name`, no `inject`, no tool registration, no settings namespace registration and no host effect registration. A City consumer imports the engine directly.

No npm packaging and no build step: no package.json, no tsconfig.json, no cordis.patch.yml, no plugin/manifest.json, no lib/ output, and no npm dependency of any kind. The only imports are `node:` built-ins.
One donor bug is reproduced deliberately rather than fixed, because every observable output must match the oracle (see `donorBugsFound`).

`bandKeyOf` for a `lower-is-worse` metric tests `value <= best` before `value <= worst`, and since `best > worst` the second test is unreachable: `:warn` is never returned for `ram_available_bytes` or `recovery_rate`. Reproduced.

The `normalizeSample` hard-bound snapping path was never asserted by the donor's own suite (acceptance gap 2). The port pins it: a value within the relative `1e-9` tolerance of the bound snaps, a value beyond it is rejected, and a value strictly inside the bound is left alone.

`resolveConfig` error messages were never asserted by the donor's own suite (acceptance gap 3). The port pins the exact message fragments for a bad band, a bad hysteresis pair, a non-ascending window list, an all-zero weight table, a malformed wall-clock string and a non-canonical metric name.
The donor's model-facing tool descriptions, the harness tool contract (`output.render`, `timeoutMs`) and `ToolDefinitionLike` are dropped. Only the strings those tools returned are kept.

The restart request's `source` field is still the literal string `'dsh-health-scheduler'`. It is a value the donor emits into the request record, the differential harness compares request objects field by field, and changing it would break parity for a cosmetic reason. It therefore names a package that no longer exists as a package. A mission that wants a Utopia-neutral requester id should change it on both sides of a future comparison, not only here.
Deferred, and not claimed: nothing. Every source path in `donors[].sourcePaths` was ported. The donor's own `src/dsh/**` binding is out of scope by mission instruction.

donorBugsFound.what: For a `lower-is-worse` metric the first test is `value <= best` and the second is `value <= worst`. Because `rampEndpoints` returns `best > worst` for that polarity, the second test can never be reached, so a lower-is-worse metric can never be timed in its `:warn` band. Measured against the compiled oracle: `bandKeyOf('ram_available_bytes', 1 GiB, {warn: 4 GiB, critical: 512 MiB})` returns `'ram_available_bytes:critical'`, and `bandKeyOf('recovery_rate', 0.5, {warn: 0.8, critical: 0.3})` returns `'recovery_rate:critical'`.
donorBugsFound.impact: The sustain gate for `ram_available_bytes` and `recovery_rate` accumulates from the warn endpoint rather than the critical endpoint, so a lower-is-worse metric that crosses from warn into critical has already satisfied its sustain gate. For every `higher-is-worse` metric the branch is correct and unaffected.
donorBugsFound.action: Reproduced exactly, not fixed: the mission is MIGRATION_ONLY and the differential harness compares band keys on both sides. Pinned by a test that says so. A fix would need a mission decision because it changes when a gate opens.

PARITY: The whole pressure model: the six dimensions, their nominal weights, the coverage renormalisation over known dimensions, and the 50/50 weighted-mean/worst-member blend
The per-metric band ramp (linear, rounded, clamped, polarity-owned) and the sustain gate
The uptime ramp over 8h..336h as the `time` dimension
The normalisation rules: canonical vocabulary, hard bounds with the relative 1e-9 tolerance, the ratio 1.0..1.5 clamp, and omission as the only encoding of unknown
The rolling store: raw retention floor, aggregates, band timing, percentiles, daily summaries
The trend analyser: sample/span/R² gates, aggregate-bucket fallback, polarity-aware worsening, projections
The policy engine: the five-rung ladder, hysteresis, debounce, dwell, the three cooldowns, min-repeat pacing, the restart gate, the state machine
Maintenance window arithmetic (local calendar, wrapping windows, all six phases) and worst-first safe-point folding
The provider registry with exponential backoff and per-provider isolation
The append-only bounded JSONL decision log with rotation and torn-tail tolerance
The provider layer's telemetry contracts: the stats-file reader, the command-probe grammar, the hardware/memory/runtime/stats-backed providers and the process-tree reader
The text and JSON report renderers
PORT_ADAPTATION: TypeScript to JSDoc-annotated ESM JavaScript; no type surface is emitted at runtime
The donor's compiled output was the transcription source, so the algorithms, constants, orderings, tolerances and strings are the donor's own bytes
Module graph flattened (one types.mjs, one providers.mjs); three private `PROVIDES` constants renamed to avoid a shared-scope collision
Private helpers promoted to exports so one entry point can express the donor's own vectors
`src/dsh/report.ts` and the presentation half of `src/dsh/plugin.ts` kept as report.mjs; the settings-watch logic kept as settings.mjs; the provider wiring kept as wiring.mjs

2-space indentation, UTOPIA file headers, Object.freeze on exported constant tables, `node:`-prefixed built-ins
UTOPIA_EXTENSION: None in behaviour. The only additions are the four module files that exist to hold logic the donor had buried inside its Cordis plugin body (report.mjs, settings.mjs, wiring.mjs, adapters.mjs) and the exports needed to reach private helpers from a flat module.
`PRESET_DOCUMENTS` exposes the donor's shipped presets/*.json as data; it is derived from files the donor already published and is asserted equal to the built presets.

The donor's npm/Cordis packaging (package.json, tsconfig.json, cordis.patch.yml, plugin/manifest.json, presets/schema.json, scripts/**) is dropped by mission instruction, not deferred.
